tool.name: find_companies
tool.title: Find companies
tool.description: In Chat, matching rows may include connectedSlackChannels with active customer-channel sync destinations. Search, list, or filter companies (accounts, organizations) by name, domain, location, owner, list, parent company, or custom properties. A string name does a case-insensitive substring search and is the default for locating a company the user names, because their wording may omit prefixes or suffixes or contain a typo. A name written as a domain (acme.com) also matches companies named after it (Acme) and companies that own that domain. Use name.$eq only when strict full-name equality is explicitly required, not merely because the user supplied a specific-looking name. Returns { resultSetId, total, rows } — use total for counts without reading all rows; pass resultSetId to add_companies_to_list, remove_companies_from_list, archive_companies instead of copying IDs. It covers every matching record (resultSetCount, up to 10,000); rows is a 5 row sample when more matched, so use query_result_set to read more, narrow, or project fields, and pass resultSetId to bulk tools to act on all matches. For list membership pass listIds only; add viewId to query a specific dynamic list view (get_list.views). Do not copy get_list filters. Use returnColumns.system to request only the company fields needed. Request relations only when their compact summaries are needed: contacts and deals return id/name; activities return id/name/time/type. Use the relevant find tool for richer related-record data. Max 500 results per page.

tool.name: add_company
tool.title: Add company
tool.description: Create one new company (account/organization). Requires a name and domain, plus optional description, LinkedIn, location, owners, lists, parent company, custom properties. Check find_companies or known context for an existing match by name/domain first and reuse it for requested contact/deal links. Create a missing company when the user's request implies it and provides enough details; ask for missing required details rather than inventing them. Resolve a requested parent company to its UUID. Refuses to create a company whose domain an existing company already uses, or whose name matches an existing company, and names that company: link to it instead. Pass distinctFromCompanyIds only after the user confirms a name match is a different organization. Creates a single record; does not search, list, or edit existing companies. tool.name: find_contacts
tool.title: Find contacts
tool.description: In Chat, matching rows may include connectedSlackChannels from a direct contact association or the contact's company. Search, find, or filter contacts (people, leads, prospects) by name, email, phone, title, company, location, LinkedIn, list, owner, or global messaging suppression. Each standard row includes email (the primary address), emails (every address the contact can be reached at, primary first), emailVerified, emailVerifiedAt, unsubscribedFromAllMessaging, and unsubscribedFromAllMessagingAt. emailVerified describes the primary address only: true means it was verified, false means it failed verification, and null means it is unverified. Secondary addresses in emails carry no verification state and are always treated as unverified when sending. unsubscribedFromAllMessaging is the system-wide opt-out flag, not a custom property. Returns { resultSetId, total, rows } — use total for counts, rows for data; pass resultSetId to add_contacts_to_list, remove_contacts_from_list, archive_contacts, or sequence audience tools instead of copying IDs. It covers every matching record (resultSetCount, up to 10,000); rows is a 5 row sample when more matched, so use query_result_set to read more, narrow, or project fields, and pass resultSetId to bulk tools to act on all matches. For list membership pass listIds only; add viewId to query a specific dynamic list view (get_list.views). Do not copy get_list filters. Use listIds for OR, allListIds for AND. Use returnColumns.system to request only the contact fields needed. Request relations only when their compact summaries are needed: company and deals return id/name; activities return id/name/time/type. Use the relevant find tool for richer related-record data. Max 500 results per page.

tool.name: find_deals
tool.title: Find deals
tool.description: In Chat, matching rows may include connectedSlackChannels from the deal or its company. Search, list, or filter deals by name, value, weighted value, stage, pipeline stage type (lead/in-progress/won/lost/active), company, contact, owner, list, created, close, start, or end date. weightedValue is the computed deal value after confidence; value is the unweighted amount. A string name does a case-insensitive substring search and is the default for locating a deal the user names, because their wording may omit prefixes or suffixes or contain a typo. Use name.$eq only when strict full-name equality is explicitly required, not merely because the user supplied a specific-looking name. If the user names a pipeline, first get its pipelineId from get_workspace_metadata and include pipelineId in the find_deals input; do not filter by stage/type alone across all pipelines. Returns { resultSetId, total, rows } — use total for counts without reading all rows (e.g. limit=1 to count a stage); pass resultSetId to add_deals_to_list, remove_deals_from_list, archive_deals instead of copying IDs. It covers every matching record (resultSetCount, up to 10,000); rows is a 5 row sample when more matched, so use query_result_set to read more, narrow, or project fields, and pass resultSetId to bulk tools to act on all matches. For list membership pass listIds only; add viewId to query a specific dynamic list view (get_list.views). Do not copy get_list filters. Use returnColumns.system to request only the deal fields needed. Request relations only when their compact summaries are needed: company and contacts return id/name; activities return id/name/time/type. Do not request company or contacts just to get companyId/contactIds, and use the relevant find tool for richer related-record data. Use pipelineStage.type 'active' to match all non-won/non-lost deals in the selected pipeline. Max 500 results per page. For 'recently added' queries, filter by createdAt.$gte. For 'recently updated or active' queries, include returnColumns.relations=['lastActivity'] and sort or filter by that.

tool.title: Verify contact emails
tool.description: Verify exact email candidates for one or more CRM contacts in a single call. Call find_contacts first. For each target, pass contactId and optionally up to 5 unsaved candidateEmails. Omit candidateEmails to recheck the saved primary address (verification state is recorded against the primary only; a contact's secondary addresses in emails have no verification state). Passing a saved secondary as a candidate checks it and, when it is the unique valid match, promotes it to primary while keeping the previous primary as a secondary. In chat, one approval shows every candidate, the total workspace credit cost, and whether a unique valid match will be saved. Each distinct email is charged at the workspace plan's email verification price, including invalid, risky, or inconclusive results; the approval shows the exact cost. A catch-all result is risky, not verified, and is never saved automatically. A single call can verify at most 100 distinct addresses.

tool.name: schedule_calendar_event
tool.title: Schedule calendar event
tool.description: Schedule a calendar event on the user's connected Google Calendar and create a calendarEvents record in Zero. Call get_calendars first. If exactly one calendar with canScheduleEvents=true is returned, use its id. If multiple calendars can schedule events, ask the user which one to use before calling this tool. If none can schedule events, explain that a supported calendar must be connected. For repeated meetings, create one recurring series with recurrence and timeZone. Check each occurrence for a finite series; for an open-ended series check the next year and explain that horizon. Before calling this tool, call find_calendar_events for the current user's id over the full calendar day of the proposed start time. Treat any event where startTime < proposedEnd and endTime > proposedStart as a conflict. If there is a conflict, pick another time or ask the user — do not schedule until the current user is free unless they explicitly accept the conflict.

startTime.description: Start time as ISO 8601 date-time with Z or an explicit UTC offset.

calendarId.description: Required ID from get_calendars for a calendar with canScheduleEvents=true. If multiple calendars can schedule events, ask the user which one to use before scheduling. Do not call this tool when none can schedule events.

companyIds.description: Optional company IDs to link to the event.

tool.title: Edit list
tool.description: Edit a list and one of its views. listFolderId moves it to a folder from list_list_folders; null removes it from its folder without changing records, views, or pins. order is an optional zero-based position in the destination folder (clamped to the end). Moves append by default; same-folder moves keep their position unless order is supplied. Affected folder orders are normalized atomically. viewId defaults to the list's default view. subGroupBy adds an optional nested second-level grouping within groupBy (requires groupBy). filters REPLACES the view filters entirely — call get_list first and send the complete new filter object. On a dynamic list filters define membership; on a regular list they only narrow what the view shows. filterBased: true with filters converts a regular list to dynamic. filterBased: false snapshots the current default view membership into a regular list, replacing old static membership; saved view filters remain as display filters. addView and removeViewId are each a call of their own and cannot be combined with any other edit. On a sequence-owned list, a view's sequence participant columns are presentation the sequence Contacts tab manages: they cannot be passed in and are kept through column edits, and the list's last contacts grid view can be neither deleted nor converted to a board.

tool.name: read_report
tool.title: Read report data
tool.description: Run a report server-side and return its computed data (a single KPI value, grouped breakdown rows, or time-series buckets). Takes exactly one of { reportId } — a saved panel from find_reports — or { config } — an unsaved report config, run as written and saved nowhere, which is how you check what a panel would show before saving it with add_report or edit_report. Returns { report, source, window, rows, rowCount } where report includes the configured relativeTimeframe/startDate/endDate, source is 'report' or 'config', and window is the range actually applied — the report's own window, resolved here. NOTE: a named window (e.g. 'this week') is resolved against the server's clock and timezone while the rendered chart resolved it against the viewer's, so a boundary bucket can differ by a day. A metric, dimension, or filter naming a native column the entity does not have fails here with the offending key; a custom-property UUID or select option key that does not exist is not validated and comes back as zero rows instead. Reading by id also returns config, the saved panel's full configuration in the same form add_report and edit_report take, so you can clone or adapt a panel instead of rebuilding it from its chart; configIssues comes with it when the stored panel does not satisfy the current config contract, and those must be fixed before that config is sent back. Saved charts can be viewed in Zero.

tool.description: Update a saved report panel. `config` fields are merged over the stored report and the merged result is validated as a whole, so a partial edit cannot leave the panel unrenderable; array/object fields (metrics, dimensions, where, settings) are replaced rather than deep-merged, so send each one complete. tool.name: import_lead_search_results
tool.title: Import lead search results into the CRM
tool.description: Add to the CRM everything a lead source matches, from exactly one source. The source decides what is written, exactly as the search's own page does: a search set to Contacts, or one carrying contact filters (titles, seniority, keywords), imports the matching people with their companies, the same people the page shows on each company row; a company-filters-only search imports companies.
